about: Look invariants: one entry per flaw the owner reported, each a view (q, a still: speed=0 is added, unless q sets the speed: then its frames are flown) with absolute measures and limits (tools/lib/measures.mjs). Fields: reported (the date), wrong (what was wrong, in one line), measures (each: measure, region [x, y, w, h] as fractions of the picture, its options, and min and/or max), bad and fixed (commits where it was bad and where it was fixed: the proof), sweep ({param, values}: one still for each value of that parameter of the page, measured together by the sweep measures), expected ('fail': a known open flaw; it is reported as KNOWN, and passing fails the run so that the mark is removed), reference (values measured on other commits, for reading only). The stills are of size (unless --size; the limits hold at this size). A limit changes only on purpose, in a commit that says why.

entries.wrong: (a guard: from 11 km looking down the picture did not brighten as the sun went down, and must not)
entries.note: The sun from 10 degrees up to 12 down (date 80, latitude 35: 10, 8, 6, 4, 2, 0, -1, -2, -3, -4, -5, -5.5, -6, -7, -8, -10, -12 degrees; the times). The largest rise of the mean luma from a still to a later one. A guard: 0.0 on main 718df06 and with the world's light.

entries.name: turn-up-gradual-40km-dusk
entries.wrong: from 40 km with the sun 4 degrees down, raising the view from the Earth to the sky closed the exposure by 2.8 stops between a view raised 15 degrees and one raised 25: it read as a switch
entries.note: Looking away from the sun, the view from 40 degrees down to 40 up in steps of 5 and 10 degrees. The exposure is window.__exposure (the adaptation, before the keys). 7fade82 (the world's light coming in between WORLD_SHARE 0.1 and 0.35): 1.6 between 20 and 25 degrees. With WORLD_SHARE[1] = 1: 0.58, between the level view and one lowered 5 degrees (5.10, 4.52; then 3.96, 3.44, 3.00, 2.67, 2.52 at 5 to 25 degrees up).

entries.name: mid-top-of-slider-40km
entries.wrong: at the top of the slider (mid=1) the middle clouds' cells left clear lakes kilometres wide: a little over half the view from 40 km was cloud, where the layer is to be nearly closed, cells with seams between them
entries.note: The white mask straight down from 40 km: 0.539 on main 03b0a75, 0.644 with MID_SHUT (the map counts a quarter at 1, the cells stand closer and higher). The seams between the cells are not in the mask.

entries.name: mid-packed-deck-11km
entries.wrong: altocumulus from 11 km looking down was equal round white puffs side by side with clear gaps between them, like polka dots on the sea, where aircraft photographs of such decks show packed cells and rolls with narrow shaded seams
entries.note: The white mask of the field's body at mid=0.8: 0.870 on main ca77500, 0.810 in the first state of #135 (the sea between the puffs), 0.985 with MID_FLOOR (the seams are thin low cloud, shaded). The measure does not see the rolls or the shade itself.

entries.name: cirrus-shadow-glow-clear-0.3km
entries.wrong: the clear sky of cirrus-shadow-glow-0.3km at the same exposure: what its cirrus is measured against

entries.name: cirrus-shadow-glow-0.3km
entries.wrong: cirrus in the Earth's shadow, seen towards the twilight glow with the sun 7 degrees down, paler and lavender against the brighter sky behind it, where photographs show dark grey streaks: the cirrus was lit by the mean light at its height, most of which is the glow on its own horizon
entries.note: The sky some 10 to 20 degrees over the glow, cirrus against the same view without it: 1.088 on e18ddb1 (85 % of the pixels lighter), 0.986 once the cirrus in the Earth's shadow takes the sky's light through its faces and the glow only through the gaps between its strands (ciSky, ciGlow).

entries.name: cirrus-lit-sun-4deg-0.3km
entries.wrong: cirrus towards the sun, 40 degrees up, with the sun 4 degrees down: grey, where photographs a few minutes after sunset show it lit pink and red: the cirrus shared the low clouds' light, which hands over from the sun to the moon between 3 and 4.5 degrees down, and had no refraction
entries.note: r/g of the brightest tenth: 1.00 on e18ddb1; 1.60 once the cirrus is lit by the sun wherever its refracted rays reach it, dimmed by their spread.

entries.name: sea-swell-lattice-4km
entries.wrong: the swell in the glitter a regular lattice: two trains of parallel crests crossing, from 1 to 11 km
entries.note: The glitter's lower half at 4 km, the sun high: spectrumPeak 1182 and regularity 1.22 with eight swells of two trains; 89 and 0.95 with 28 spread over their directions and lengths, in groups, and the patches of rougher and smoother water.

entries.name: sea-glitter-even-11km
entries.wrong: from 11 km the sea smooth below 10 m/s of wind, and the sun's glitter an even blur; photographs from cruise show it mottled by patches of rougher and smoother water
entries.note: The glitter's lower part with the sun 15 degrees up: texture 0.022 even, 0.036 mottled.

entries.name: sea-whitecap-blobs-0.3km
entries.wrong: whitecaps flat white blobs on dark water, without foam trailing behind them
entries.note: Foam beside the white per white pixel: 1.13 with blobs alone, 1.70 with trails torn into streaks behind them.

entries.name: twilit-earth-hue-40km
entries.wrong: from 40 km with the sun 3 degrees down, the Earth below was a saturated navy blue, where photographs from orbit show the twilit Earth blue-grey to pale blue (issue #145)
entries.note: The blue over the green of the whole frame in linear light (the page's power 2.2): 2.82 on main b6f2dea (2.97 at cda9faa, before the stratosphere's dim key); 1.84 with the twilight balance held as far as the Earth gives the metered light. ISS photographs of twilit cloud and ground: 1.2 to 2.0 (ISS027-E-012224, ISS002-E-7377, ISS059-E-11742, ISS063-E-53859; their white balance unknown). 96 % of the Earth's light here is the air's.

entries.name: twilit-earth-hue-20km
entries.wrong: the same from 20 km (issue #145)
entries.note: As twilit-earth-hue-40km: 2.41 on main b6f2dea, 1.58 fixed.

entries.name: day-sky-blue-up-11km
entries.wrong: kept: the deep blue of the sky by day from cruise, which a twilight correction of the colour must not reach (issue #145)
entries.note: 4.42 on main b6f2dea and with the fix: by day the balance is a camera's for daylight at every height.

entries.name: dusk-sky-blue-away-11km
entries.wrong: kept: from cruise with the sun 4 degrees down, the sky away from the sun stays pale blue (round 10: with the twilight balance in full it turned grey)
entries.note: The sky's upper 30 %: 2.70 on main b6f2dea; 2.34 with the fix, where the Earth gives about a third of the metered light. Round 10 found this sky grey with the twilight balance in full at this height.

entries.name: mid-rolls-even-40km
entries.wrong: the middle clouds' rolls (?midrolls) from 40 km were smears: long lumps that began and ended anywhere, with no distance of their own from one to the next, where photographs show rolls packed side by side at an even distance, with narrow seams, that bend, fork and end
entries.note: Straight down over a region of rolls. The mean of the upper quarter of the windows. #135 at 7b0a747 (the noise drawn out one way): rollEven 0.18, rollLong 2.35; the map of rolls grown by the Swift-Hohenberg equation: 0.41 and 3.57. Photographs of rolls from orbit, scaled to rolls as many pixels apart: 0.44 and 3.4 (ISS023-E-10682), 0.21 and 2.7 (ISS-36, whose rolls differ more in width). The upper limit: a wave as even as a grating is near 1.

entries.name: mid-rolls-streets-40km
entries.wrong: the altocumulus weather from 40 km was fields of round cells alone: no field of it stood in rolls or streets, as fields of altocumulus do in photographs from aircraft and from orbit
entries.note: The weather as the page draws it (rolls in about half the map's regions, in groups among the cells; streets with clear air between them where the cells stand wide apart). #135 at 7b0a747 (cells alone): rollEven 0.10, rollLong 1.91; with the rolls: 0.29 and 3.34.

entries.name: mid-rolls-lattice-40km
entries.wrong: the view of mid-lattice-40km with every region in rolls: rolls must not make the layer a lattice or ruled lines to the horizon (waves did: a peak of 49; the noise drawn out one way 35)
entries.note: The limit of mid-lattice-40km. #135 at 7b0a747 with ?midrolls=1: 35.0; the map of rolls: 29.4 (27.7 in mid-lattice-40km's own view, rolls in half the regions; 26.7 there at 7b0a747). Far off, where the map no longer tells the rolls apart, the cells take over: with rolls to the horizon the groups were bands 32 px apart there, a peak of 39 to 55.

entries.name: cirrus-fibres-under-deck-11.5km
entries.wrong: cirrus seen from just under its sheet a smooth gradient, a grey blurred fan with no fibres: the ice has nothing finer than some 100 m, and every fine term faded over the step's length along the ray (issue #9)
entries.note: The detail of 3 to 17 px over the sky: 0.003 on main a2ba547 (satin), 0.026 with the fibres (ciFibre; 0.041 in their first round, as thin bright threads), read with the pixel's footprint at the sheets of the march.

entries.name: cirrus-fibres-ground-0.3km
entries.wrong: cirrus from the ground at a high sun airbrushed strokes with a satin inside: no fibres within the forms (issue #9)
entries.note: 0.011 on main a2ba547, 0.030 with the fibres.

entries.name: cirrus-edge-frays-11km
entries.wrong: the dense patch of cirrus at the top left of the default view ended on one smooth rounded curve, like a cumulus top (issue #9: 'its boundary shows clearly')
entries.note: The outline's length over that of the smoothed picture's: 1.20 on main a2ba547 (a clean envelope), 1.79 with the fibres, which shape thin ice most.

entries.name: sheet-sunset-up-0.3km
entries.wrong: an altostratus overhead with the sun 1.5 degrees up an even salmon wall, where photographs show the sheet slate grey to blue-grey, warm only low towards the sun
entries.note: Linear light over the frame: r/g 1.473, b/g 0.814 on main 3678899 (the sun's light on the sheet by a cosine of no less than 0.2, 7 times what a sun 1.5 degrees up brings a level plane); 0.848 and 1.304 with the sun's height alone and the camera's balance under the sheet. Photographs of altostratus overhead near sunset (Wikimedia Commons, Famartin, CC BY-SA 4.0): blue over green 1.28 to 1.32 as shown where the sun is at or under the horizon, 1.01 where it is grey.

entries.name: sheet-sunset-away-4km
entries.wrong: the same from 4 km away from the sun at 0 degrees: the sheet salmon from the base to the horizon, lit from below where the sun stood under the level at its place, through no cloud
entries.note: Linear light over the upper half: r/g 1.738 on main 3678899 (the base lit from below wherever the sun stood under the level at its place, and by the cosine's floor from above); 0.741 with the light from below through the layer where it went down through it (midSlant) and the sun's height alone.

entries.name: sheet-horizon-noon-0.3km
entries.wrong: under an altostratus at noon from 0.3 km the sheet turned cream towards the horizon, where photographs go grey to blue-grey and darker
entries.note: Linear light over the band above the horizon: b/g 0.918, r/g 1.096 on main 3678899 (the far base as bright aslant as overhead, the haze before it taking away the blue of its light and giving back less); 0.995 and 1.056 with the light through the slab darker aslant (limb, Eddington's 0.5 + 0.75 cos). Photographs of altostratus towards the horizon by day: 1.2 to 1.28 and 0.90 to 0.93, constant or bluer and darker towards the horizon.

entries.name: dusk-earth-shadow-away-11km
entries.wrong: from cruise, away from a sun 3.5 degrees down, the Earth in its shadow stood too light and too red under the sky (the dusk audit of issue #40, items 1 and 2)
entries.note: The table of multiple scattering read straight between its columns (2 degrees of the sun apart) held 1.3 to 1.4 times too much light here, and its light was taken as even where it comes level from the glow. The reference (tools/ref): the air under the horizon 1.03 to 1.3 times too bright (green) and up to 1.8 times in the red on 393b81c, 0.9 to 1.16 with the fix. As shown: sky over ground 1.73 on 393b81c, 1.92 fixed. It holds a ratio within one still, so that the exposure and most of the balance cancel.

entries.name: dusk-earth-shadow-side-11km
entries.wrong: to the side of a sun 5 degrees down the air under the horizon was 1.4 to 1.5 times the reference's (issue #40: side views in deep twilight too bright)
entries.note: Clear air, so that only the air and the sea are measured. Sky over ground 1.39 on 393b81c, 1.61 fixed; against the reference the air under the horizon 1.4 to 1.5 before, 0.97 to 1.08 now.

entries.name: sunset-never-brighter-away-11km
entries.wrong: from cruise, away from the sun, the picture grew brighter again as the sun went from 4 to 4.25 and from 6 to 6.25 degrees down (the knee of the time-lapse in the dusk audit of issue #40)
entries.note: The sun from 3.5 to 6.5 degrees down in steps of a quarter degree. The table of multiple scattering held up to 1.4 times too much light half way between its columns (2 degrees of the sun apart), so the air's light fell unevenly: the frame's mean rose by 1.3 levels at 4.25 degrees and 1.4 at 6.25 on 393b81c; it falls at every step with the fix.

entries.name: sea-shadow-11km-down25
entries.wrong: from 11 km nothing ties the heaps to the sea: no shadow shows on the water outside the sun's glitter (#156)
entries.note: No measure of a still separates the two: the shadow is a few percent of the sea's light, less than the glitter's mottle and the gradients across the frame (patchStops less the best plane 0.455 and 0.454; a block's dip under the blocks around it 0.116 and 0.123). Measured with the shadow's own picture from a patched copy of the page (the sea where the light let through is under 0.1, against the lit sea within 25 px, linear luminance as shown): 0.932 on main 393b81c, 0.916 with the light that the clouds let down diffusely (seaThrough); photographs from aircraft and from orbit outside the glitter under a high sun: 0.85 to 0.94, and none seen from 11 km over small heaps. Kept for the contact sheet.

entries.name: dusk-ground-sky-cool-0.3km
entries.wrong: near the sea towards the sun with the sun 2 degrees down, the clear sky 15 to 25 degrees up was grey-mauve (the twilight white balance warmed it), where photographs show it cooler, blue-grey to lavender (issue #40, item 3)
entries.note: The sky 15 to 25 degrees up, across the middle of the frame, in linear light (the page's power 2.2).

entries.name: low-sun-side-sky-blue-0.3km
entries.wrong: near the sea with the sun on the horizon, the clear sky at the side lost its blue (red over green about 0.9 in linear light), where photographs of a low sun's sky give 0.34 to 0.46: the camera kept daylight's balance under the reddened sun (issue #40, item 4)
entries.note: The sky 15 to 25 degrees up, linear (the page's power 2.2). Photographs (cumulus at sunset, the clear sky beside them): 0.34 to 0.46.

entries.name: twilit-earth-hue-30km-2deg
entries.wrong: from 30 km looking down with the sun 2 degrees down, the twilit Earth was mauve-brown (red over green 1.5 in linear light), where frames from orbit give 0.86 to 1.02 (issue #40, item 3)

entries.name: twilit-earth-hue-30km-6deg
entries.wrong: from 30 km looking down, the twilit Earth turned navy (blue over green 3.1 at 6 degrees down, 3.9 at 9) as the twilight balance's window let go, where frames from orbit give 1.2 to 1.5 (issue #40, item 3)

entries.name: twilit-earth-hue-30km-9deg
entries.wrong: the same at 9 degrees down: navy (blue over green 3.9 in linear light)
